utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the sheet shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Regue. You're to take this witness, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We're calling Mr. Sherafedin Ajrullai.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ajrullai.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in September 2004?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting with a lady from the registry who certified, put a stamp on your statement in 2005?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read your statement before coming here today in Court?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the statement that you read was correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will seek to tender this witness's statement pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P403, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The witness, Mr. Sherafedin Ajrullai, is a Macedonian citizen of Albanian ethnicity and a Ljuboten resident. Between 10 to 12 August, 2001, the witness saw and heard shooting and shelling towards Ljuboten. As a consequence, the witness and his family sought shelter in a neighbour's basement. Around 5.00 p.m. On 12 August, 2001, the witness and his family decided to leave Ljuboten and saw houses burning in the upper part of the village. On their way to Skopje, they were stopped by the police near the check-point and then at the check-point itself. The police search and beat the witness and other Albanian villagers there. They were then taken by police jeep to Butel or Cair police station where they were forced to walk through a gauntlet of masked police who beat them before entering the building. The witness and the fellow villagers were also beaten at the actual police station. After midnight, the witness and the others were transported to Karpos police station, around 40 to 50 Ljuboten villagers were being held there and were also maltreated. The witness was submitted to the paraffin test and was told that he had been tested positive. Nevertheless, he and others were then taken by police jeep to a building near the court-house in Skopje and released on the street. After walking 50 metres, other police officers approached them and beat them before taking them to Bit Pazar police station where they were beaten again. They were released after the intervention of a senior police officer from Bit Pazar police station in the early hours of 13 August 2001. The witness still suffers headaches and chest pains as a result of this mistreatment. Mr. Ajrullai, after you were released in August 2001, were you ever interviewed by any member of the Macedonian police or the minister of interior about what happened in Ljuboten in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we can have, please, displayed in e-court, 65 ter 199.33. It's page 545, ERN N004-4984. Your Honours, it's the same photo but a bit enlarged of the one you can find in page 18, photo B of the court binder. It is enlarged as well. Mr. Ajrullai, what do you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: This is the police station in Butel, from the back side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your statement, you describe that you were taken to this police station on Sunday, 12th of August, and you were forced to walk through two lines of policemen?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If we could have, please, the usher's assistance. Are you able to see the place where the two lines of policemen were located that day? Are you able to see it?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: If could you please draw a line indicating where the policemen were standing.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Here, they were lined up here, in two lines and this is where they beat us and where they forced us inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: For the record the witness has drawn a line in the centre of the photo on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I'll seek to tender this photo into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P404, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ajrullai.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic and I appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. I would like to ask you, Mr. Ajrullai, to wait a while when I ask a question, to wait until it is interpreted in your language as well as the English language so that the Bench and the colleagues in the courtroom are able to know what am I asking you and what is your reply to me. In that way, I think we will be of the best assistance for the Bench to follow your testimony. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai, you were born in Ljuboten and you live there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I was born in Skopje, but I live in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You graduated from a school for car mechanics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No. I only worked as one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you used to work as a car mechanic, although in 2001, you still hadn't finished that school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I only worked as a car mechanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that in your statement you were a bit more precise, but that is not of great significance. You just stated before this Court what was your occupation. Tell me, please, were you employed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001 you were married already, and you lived with your wife and with two children in your family house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you gave your testimony, your statement to the investigator of the OTP, you had two children, a son and a daughter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have three children now; you have one more daughter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ajrullai, that on the 10th of August, 2001, not far from your village at the Ljubotenski Bacila locality, a land-mine planted by the NLA members killed eight and injured several more soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know about this. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know about this, you did not see it. Is that that you didn't see it or you are not aware of the fact at all?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I didn't see it, but I heard of it on the news.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that as soon as you learned about the news, you could see that fire started towards the village, fire of bullets and grenades on the Friday, 10th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that some of the villagers of Ljuboten participated in the planting of this mine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that after the mine explosion three armed people entered the village of Ljuboten. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, as a young person from that village, you were at the age of persons who were fit to serve the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question? I'm not clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before 2001, you served in the army of the Republic of Macedonia, and after that, you continued to be a military reservist in the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it once again, because I cannot understand the interpretation very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that people of age 18 and above are military reservists, in most of the states, and particularly, they are military reservists in the Republic of Macedonia? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it -- the translation says military reservists, I'm not speaking about reservists, I'm speaking about conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the other young people after you have served the conscript military service, you continued to be a conscript; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I was a soldier of the Republic of Macedonia when I completed my military service, my obligation towards the country. After that, I didn't receive any invitation to join.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you never joined NLA either, or UCK, although you were aware that, at that time, the crisis involved fights between the NLA and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Once again, please. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, you were aware that in certain regions of the Republic of Macedonia there were fights between the NLA and the army of the Republic of Macedonia and the police forces. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it on the news.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not join NLA at any moment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you were aware that quite a number of young people from the village of Ljuboten joined NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I didn't see any of them in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But although did you not see them, you knew that quite a number of young people from the village of Ljuboten joined NLA. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm not aware of any being members.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you did not understand what I was asking. I know that you were not a member. And you don't know of any other people who would have been NLA members; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I don't know of any others. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 10th of August, after the mine exploded at Ljubotenski Bacila, fire started towards the village from the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia from the -- from north of the village?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were at the street and you were able to see the bullets hitting the street and the houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you knew, because the positions of the army were even before that event in the hills above the village, that the fire came from the army positions. You couldn't see who was firing only. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And because of the bullets that were hitting the street, you and an older man took shelter behind a house wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your house is a bit further from the graveyard at about 100, 150 metres towards the school in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you can testify before this Court that at that time most of the houses in Ljuboten were built in the traditional way, and that the yards were fenced with walls; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Please repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that most of the houses in Ljuboten are built in the traditional Albanian way, so this means that -- that the space of the courtyard was fenced with a wall facing the street, in order to protect the privacy of the family living in that house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: The walls are built because the population are mainly dealing with agriculture, with tobacco and they need the walls to dry the tobacco. That's why they built those walls and that's why they're there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And most of the houses had those walls; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you and that old man actually hid behind such wall, in order to save yourself from the bullets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The walls erected around the houses, in that way also, would not let the people passing down the street see what is going on in the houses and inside the courtyard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, that's not so. I told you already that the walls are there to dry the tobacco because the -- they mainly cultivate tobacco.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that if you're walking down the street five in Ljuboten, regardless of the fact there is a wall, you could see whatever happens in the yard of a house, or are you not able to see anything?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Of course you are. No, no, you cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all that I wanted to say. Tell me, please, Mr. Ajrullai, is it also correct that the houses are mainly built terraced in a row and that within a neighbourhood there are mainly members of a family, people in blood relation live. For instance, families such as Jusufi, Zendeli, Bajrami, Durmisina, is that correct, that the closer or the broader family members live next to one another and this is way in which they built their houses. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you just mentioned a moment ago that people there mainly deal in agriculture, and it is customary that all the farming machines are in the courtyard, such as tractors, the oil, then the hay, the cattle, everything is there. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to put to you that if, for instance, the stable where hay was as well would be caught by fire or if the oil for the tractor would be caught by fire, and if there were no one to fight the fire, the fire would very quickly spread on to the house and the other houses located nearby; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: If it is nearby, of course it will catch fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that on Friday afternoon with your family, so with your wife and the children you went to the house of Sulejman Zendeli where there were already 30 people there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You went there because the house of Sulejman Zendeli had a better and a larger basement than yours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed there all the way until Sunday afternoon. That would be the 12th of August, the afternoon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed there till Sunday 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were there at the basement, you and other men from the basement would go in front of the house or around the house several times, in order to see what was happening in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, we were there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but I did not understand this. Did you go out many times, out from the basement, to check what was going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: We just went out when we had personal needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if in your statement, in the item 6, you stated: [In English] "We stayed there from Friday afternoon till Sunday 5.00 p.m., Sulejman's house is close to mine. I went out to the yard a few time to check what was going on, but I couldn't see anything special." [Interpretation] Then this would not be the truth. Then you stated something that was not the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: When I went out, I looked around, of course, but I saw nothing special. I saw only flames and bullets, when the bullets hit the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you told me a while ago that did you not go out to see what was going on, that was not the complete truth. You did go out and you were observing -- actually, you wanted to observe to see what was going on in the village?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I went out for my personal needs, and it's normal for me to look around.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But that is different from what you stated in your statement, that you had gone out several times to check what was going on, to see what was going on. That is different from what you are saying now. Do you agree with me regarding this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: When I went out, I looked around. This is normal. I went out for my personal needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And other people, other men who were there in the basement also went out, outside of the house to see what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you could not see anyone else going out or is it that no one else went out? Which of the two is correct? Were you the only one that went out?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I'm speaking to you about myself. When I had a problem, I went out. I went out and then I looked around, and then I came back to the basement. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also said that you could not notice much; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I saw only flames, nothing else. I saw flames at the corner of the village, things which were burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If in item 6 of your statement which you have given to the Prosecutor, you said that: [In English] "I went out to the yard a few times to check what was going on, but I couldn't see anything special. I could only hear that the shooting and shelling was going on." [Interpretation] This would be something different than what you're saying now. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I saw nothing special. I saw only flames and smoke, smoke coming out of the grenades and bullets they were shooting at. I went out for my personal needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this smell and the smoke which was coming from the shooting and the shells, it came from all sides. You heard that there was shooting towards the village and from the village. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: From the hill in the direction of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "from the hill," do you mean that this is the same hill from which you heard that there was shooting on Friday as well?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: From the place called Manastir, they shoot from there and then the shells hit the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that on Sunday at 5.00 p.m., that you left the house; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, you left that house because at that time, for the first time, you noticed that a number of houses in the upper part of the village were on fire; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: We went because they were being burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is it correct that you left the house of Zendeli Sulejman because at that moment you noticed that a number of houses in the upper part of the village were on fire?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to this, you did not notice any house on fire; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I was in the basement. I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then when you were leaving on a number of occasions from the basement, you also didn't notice that some houses were on fire; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I went out of the basement at night. I could not come out during the day because of the bullets. I could not come out during the day. I went out only at night quickly, had my personal needs finished, and then I came inside again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when, on Sunday afternoon, around 5.00 p.m., you saw in the upper part of the village several houses on fire, this was really a few houses. Can you tell us the number? Were there three houses, four houses? Can you recall the number of houses which you saw on fire?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, you remember that it was a small number of houses; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember this at all. I went out quickly, and then I got into the car and went off quickly. It was night, and I didn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At 5.00 p.m., in August, in Ljuboten, it's nightfall, is this what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, it was not dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it was not dark when you sat in the car and left the village?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, with your wife, two children, and your mother moved on. You left together?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: My mother did not come with me. I went only with my wife. Halfway we met another woman and we took her with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you left with your Golf I, red in colour; is this correct? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I was with a Golf.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you left towards Butel where the father of your wife lived; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your brother Hazbi Ajrullai also left the village with his vehicle.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not far --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, there is no answer to my previous question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I wish -- I would ask you to respond. Is it correct that your brother Hazbi Ajrullai left the village with his own car?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: He left after me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you came close to the place Kodra e Zajmit, or as Macedonians call it, Zaimovo Brdo, here for the first time were checked, your documents were checked by the police. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Before we reached the point, we were stopped and they checked us. They behaved very badly with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, this point, Kodra e Zajmit, is it correct that is about three, four kilometres far from the -- from Buzalak?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. From Buzalak, I don't know. It could be two, it could be three. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in any event, these two places are not the same. They are removed several kilometres one from another?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the way to the point where you were stopped, there were many civilians from the village of Radisani on the road, as well as, in the area around the road and on the point itself; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were coming closer to the check-point, you could see many civilians from the village of Radisani who were around the road on which you were moving, on the road itself, and in -- on the check-point itself; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: There were citizens of Ljuboten. They were not people from Radishan. I did not see any of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to put it to you that these civilians were at that place and that they were wearing hunting guns, shovels and other things and they were pulling Albanians who were moving down the road, putting them down on the ground and beating them, would you agree with me that this is so?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say to you that on the road, along the road and on the check-point itself that there were many civilians from Radisani who were carrying hunting guns, cramps and other things which they pulled out the villagers who were moving along the road from the road, threw them on the ground and beat them, this would be correct. Is this so?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I didn't see these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, if I were to say to you that some of these civilians had also Molotov cocktails in their hands, would this also be true?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No. I didn't see such things. I could not speak to you about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at this check-point, in addition to you, Halil Ajrullai was also there, Sulejman Zendeli, brothers Suat, Bejtulla and Adem Zendeli, could you concur with this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your brother also came there, Hazbi Ajrullai; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your brother could also notice the civilians that I was just talking to you about; is this correct? If they were there, of course.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm suggesting, I'm putting to you that on the road, around the road and at the check-point there were civilians from Radisani. You said that you did not see this. I'm now asking you: Was your brother there? You responded that he was there. I then am putting to you that if these civilians that I was telling you were -- were there, then your brother must have also had to see this. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: This witness cannot speak for what his brother saw or could have seen and the question has been asked several times already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The second point is well made.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness confirmed that his brother was there. I'm talking about a large number of civilians from the Radisani village, and I would point to the witness the statement of his brother, to see whether the witness can, in fact, recall what in fact happened at the check-point and around the check-point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the witness says he didn't see these things, if I understand him correctly. You can put to him, Well, does it change your position if your brother did see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It really can't get much clearer than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Due to these reasons -- thank you. I wanted to see whether he knew that his brother was there. I would ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 65 ter 1D502, page 1D4592. This is the English version and this is point 4, item 4 in question. The Albanian is Exhibit 1D4601.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you this text? I would ask you to look in item 4, the last sentence where your brother Hazbi -- my apologies. Was your -- is Hazbi Ajrullai your brother?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at this last sentence where he says: [In English] "When we were stopped, I saw that my cousins and uncles had been stopped there too. I remember that my brother Sherafedin was there, as well as, my uncle Halil Ajrullai, Sulejman Zendeli and brothers Suat, Bejtulla and Adem Zendeli. They were all, of course, with their families." [Interpretation] Is -- this, in fact, not what you said that all of these people were at the check-point where you, too, were present. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: This is what my brother said me, not me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, a few minutes earlier, I asked you whether your brother Halil Ajrullai, Sulejman Zendeli and the brothers Sulejman and Zendeli were at the same place and you agreed with this. Does this mean that they were not there then?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: They were there, but if you want to check about what my brother said you better ask my brother, not me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you to respond to my questions if you know the answer to the questions that I'm putting to you, and I would be grateful for this. I would now ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 1D502, page 1D4593, and in the Albanian Exhibit 1D4602, item 6. I would ask that you look at the middle of this item, which begins with the words and then goes on: [In English] "However, I could notice that there are lots of civilians from the village of Radishan in the field next to the road in the area of the check-point and the place where the police had first stop us. The civilian were carrying hunting rifles, sticks, axes and other items in their hands and they managed to get some Albanian from the road, dragged them to the field and beat them up there. I remember that some of the civilian also had Molotov cocktails in their hands. Obviously, they had heard that OSCE was planning to bring some busses to take us away and the Molotov cocktails were there to prevent this from happening. I saw Ace Milenkovski, the mayor of Cair, was in the field among the civilians. I'm 100 per cent sure it was him. I knew him and I have even voted for him once in the election." [Interpretation] Do you think that your brother has reasons to say things which he did not see?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know. Ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I read to you the statement of your brother, can you now recall that on the road, around the road and at the check-point there were civilians from the village of Radisani, armed with all of these things which your brother listed?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I told you that I have not seen them. As for the declarations by my brother, ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you came in front of the station in Butel, also there were a lot of civilians there is too; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these civilians were armed with various weapons; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I only saw some civilians. I saw them in passing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you saw these civilians who were shouting and attacking you which the police carried towards the Police Station Butel?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please make the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These civilians which were in the vicinity of the police station in Butel were shouting and shooting towards you, villagers, brought in by the police into the police station of Butel.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I did not see them hitting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the police, as was the case at the check-point, attempted and prevented the civilians from beating the villagers; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: As for the police, there were civilian policemen there and the police stopped these civilians you are talking about. The civilians wanted to get inside, but the police did not allow them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that it is too late but in the question I can see there are two questions actually. The police of my learned friend she asked and the police as was the case at the check-point attempted and prevented the civilians, this witness never testified that the police at the check-point attempted and prevented civilians. I would just ask to -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I think the answer has made clear the position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, actually, if I were to put to you, Mr. Ajrullai, that there was no line of police officers in front of the Butel police station. It was actually civilians who attempted to attack the villagers while the police officers tried to prevent them from attacking the villagers that would be the actual truth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, it's not. When they took us to the police station, there were two columns of policemen, and we entered the police station as they were hitting us. We entered the cellar of the police station while they were hitting us, the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ajrullai -- no, I will ask you a different question first. You know probably that the paraffin glove test is taken in order to ascertain whether there is presence of gun powders or other nitrate particles on the hands of a certain person. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that paraffin glove test is often taken in order to ascertain whether on the hands of that person there are gunpowder or other nitrate particles present. Are you generally aware of this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the Karpos police station, you were submitted to that paraffin glove test; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I couldn't even look up because of them. I don't know what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They told you that they are taking the test in order to see whether you were holding weapons in your arms and whether you were shooting, and you said you never held any weapons since leaving the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police officers that gave you the paraffin glove test told you that they wanted to ascertain whether you were firing from any weapons, but you said that you hadn't ever since you left the army of the Republic of Macedonia. That was the sequence of events?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Maybe I've said that, but -- because of the beating, as a result of the beating. They did carry out the paraffin glove test, but that's not the way they should do it. I was beaten. My head was down under the table and my hands were on the table. I couldn't even look up. That's not the way to carry out a paraffin glove test.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you know that in order to get the result of this test, one needs to perform the laboratory analysis. You could not immediately know whether the test is positive or not.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And since you did not fire any weapon, you were released. You were let to go home. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: You're right, released, after I was beaten to pieces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were released, some police officers met you on the street, as you stated, and you were again taken to the Bit Pazar police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then you were incarcerated only because you did not have any personal documents on you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: After we were released, we were told to walk straight, not on the left or the right. They said, If you look on the left or to the right, we will kill you. As soon as we set off, we were stopped by other set of policemen. We were not allowed to say a word. They made us lay on the ground. Then a van, a police van came, and they took us to Bit Pazar where they beat us too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you were released from Bit Pazar, you went to your father-in-law, to your wife's father, in Skopje, to the Butel settlement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I didn't go on that same night. The night I was released, I went to my uncle, to a relative, my father's uncle, that is. And from there I was taken to the hospital, private hospital called Viktoria. I was administered an injection, because I was not -- I was not conscious, and then I was prescribed some medicine. In the morning, I went to my father-in-law's place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. Tell me, please, before 2001, you knew what a baseball bat was and you must have seen one.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: It is a bat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw that it was a rather dangerous instrument; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I had never seen one before. The first time was there at the police station where they beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, as a grown-up, you also know that if someone is jumping on to persons who are lying on the ground, especially if it is grown-up men, then those persons on to whom someone is jumping must sustain severe injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If a grown-up is jumping on a person who is lying on the ground, then certainly that person would sustain severe injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I really don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would kick a person, would kick wearing military boots, or if jumps onto someone, stomps onto someone while wearing military boots -- army boots, then certainly that person, the victim, would sustain severe injuries. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Of course he will sustain injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The doctor you went to see in that private hospital, Viktoria, administered an injection and did not find any severe injuries on you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I was not conscious when I went to the hospital. I know that I was administered an injection, and then I regained consciousness, and the doctor said to me, Don't worry, you will recover. And then I did some X-rays, but I don't know where they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have no medical documents testifying about some severe injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I was X-rayed, but I don't know where they can be found now. What else can I say? I have pain all over my body. I forget. My head is aching.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you that your entire testimony about those severe beatings with baseball bat, about the police officers jumping on your back while you were lying on the ground, and about them hitting you and jumping on you, stomping on you while wearing army boots, that would not be correct. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Everything is correct. Everything I've said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you came to your father-in-law's house and all the way until today, is it correct that you never went to any police station nor to the Ministry of the Interior to report the persons who allegedly beat you on that -- those days, 12 and 13 of August?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you never filed any criminal report against a known perpetrator or against an unknown perpetrator to the public prosecutor's office in Skopje or in any other place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I didn't file any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you never complained to the committee that the Ministry of the Interior established in order to establish any abuse of office on the part of the police officers against the Albanian population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you never filed a complaint with the committee of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Macedonia that was established in order to examine, investigate any improper conduct of the police towards the Albanian population. Is it correct that you never filed such report?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I never filed any report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never wrote to the committee for petitions of citizens within the Assembly of the Republic of Macedonia that you were treated improperly or cruelly by any of the police officers on August 12 and 13. Is it also correct that you never petitioned the parliament in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: No, I never petitioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You simply did not want to talk to the police and the authorities of Macedonia because you did not trust them then and you do not trust them now today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't trust them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And already two or three days later, you spoke to representatives of the international community, and it was only them and the investigator of this Tribunal that you spoke with about your experiences during those two days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Two or three days after you were released, you spoke first with the representatives, with some representatives of the international community, and, after that, you gave your statement to the investigator of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember when I gave these statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I refresh your memory? In your statement that was received in evidence today as your testimony, you stated: [In English] "Two or three days after the events in Ljuboten, I was interviewed about then by a representative of some organization in an office in Caircanka shopping centre. I know that the man who interviewed me was speaking French but I can't recall the name of the organization." Is it correct, then, that you gave a statement to some international organization very soon after your release?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I don't remember the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you gave a statement to the investigator of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you were convinced that that international organization to which you gave your statement, as well as the investigator of the ICTY, will take steps, and if it is necessary, they would inform the Macedonian authorities about the contents of your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you believe, when giving your statement to that international organization and the ICTY investigator, that they are the organs that should investigate this and then inform, if it is needed, the Macedonian authorities? Was that your belief and was that why you gave a statement to them?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I still don't understand your question. Please repeat it once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you gave statements to an international organization - you don't remember which one - and to the ICTY investigator. Do you remember saying this to me?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: It is true that I gave statements to some who were speaking French. I don't know whether they were from ICTY or from somewhere else, but there were two persons speaking French. This is what I remember. I gave a statement to them. But I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I understood and thank you for that. After that, in 2004, you also were invited, summonsed by the investigator of this Court and to that investigator you gave your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I did give a statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So on two occasions you spoke with some foreign organizations about what you experienced on August 12 and 13; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I were to refresh your memory again and tell that you in your statement that you verified as accurate today, you stated that two or three days after the events in Ljuboten you were interviewed by a representative of some international organization at Caircanka shopping centre, and you then stated: "I know I was interviewed by a French-speaking person, but I do not remember the name of the organization," then what you said was true. The first statement you gave was two or three days after the events in Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't know how many days after the events I gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you gave a statement, as much you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you do not remember even after my showing you that?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember how many days after the events. I did give a statement. I remember them speaking in French, but I don't know how many days after the events this happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this clarification. So my question now is: Is it correct that you described to these French-speaking foreigners and later in 2004 to the ICTY investigator, you described those events to them because you trusted them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that your belief was that it would be these organisations that would, if necessary, inform the Macedonian authorities about it all?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I have faith in The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm asking you: Is it correct that neither these French-speaking representatives of some international organization nor the ICTY investigator later instructed you that you needed to go to court to report these events. Would that also be the truth? Is it correct that these people never told you that you needed to go to court to report what has happened to you?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did these French-speaking people tell you that you needed to go to the court or to the Office of the Prosecutor and describe everything that has happened to you? Did they tell you this or did they not tell this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you mean the Macedonian court or the Macedonian prosecutor? I think that may not be clear to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did these French-speaking people who interviewed you several days after the event in Ljuboten tell you that it would be needed for you to go to Skopje, to the court, or to the prosecutor's office and tell your story about what has happened to you, or was that not their suggestion?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: They didn't say anything to me. They just asked me about the events, to describe what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the ICTY investigator asked you in 2004 about the event, did the investigator tell you then that it would be advisable for you to file a criminal report or to go to the court in Skopje or to the prosecutor's office in Skopje and tell your story there, or was it that you were not told anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: Please, could you ask me shorter questions because I don't understand these long questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I thank you for asking me clearer questions and I will do exactly that. Did the ICTY investigator, in 2004, inform you or suggest to you that you could go to the court or to the prosecutor's office in Skopje and then report to them or tell your story there, or were you not told anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: SHERAFEDIN AJRULLAI
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do not remember this. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, this question has been asked several times and we would like to know also the relevance of this question, concerning the ICTY ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the relevance is apparent enough. But the question -- I think the witness has made clear his position. He was simply asked what occurred. He was not advised either in 2001 or 2004 to go to authorities in Macedonia. And I think that is what you wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you very much. I have finished the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that's a very good time for us to have a break, and we will resume at 20 past 4.00. We will have a break now and we'll continue in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has been informed that the witness who is currently testifying is not well. He is suffering a severe stomach pain and the Victims and Witness Section is not sure what the cause is, but he is unable to continue this afternoon. The Prosecution has brought the next scheduled witness, Mr. Murati, to The Hague today. However, we are also told by the Victims and Witness Section that is Mr. Murati is simply exhausted. He got up very, very early this morning, has been travelling and that it would be much wiser for Mr. Murati to provide his testimony tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Fortunately, these two witnesses are each relatively brief so it ought, I would think, to be possible to finish the present witness, if he is recovered, and to deal with the next witness in the course of tomorrow and that would appear to be the most practical course. I see all counsel nodding. So I think that is what we must do. We hope the witness has just got some temporary problem. He seemed to be not entirely himself near the end of his evidence, so ... We will therefore adjourn, resuming tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, and we will, I hope, be able to hear both witnesses and conclude their evidence in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.39 p.m.,
